newsitem.title: USA: Stone sees 1997 Q1 better than 1996 Q4.
newsitem.headline: Stone sees 1997 Q1 better than 1996 Q4.

text.p: Stone Container Corp expects to report better results for the first quarter of 1997 than it did in the fourth quarter of 1996, Roger Stone, chairman, president and chief executive officer, told Reuters.
"We reached the trough in newsprint and containerboard (pricing), but I'm not so sure on pulp," Stone said in a telephone interview.
Stone said his remarks on the first quarter echoed those made earlier Tuesday to analysts in a teleconference. He would not elaborate.

On Monday, the paper and packaging company reported a fourth-quarter loss of $0.89 a share against a year-ago profit of $0.73 a diluted share. The 1995 results included extraordinary charges of $0.07 a diluted share.
Smith Barney analyst George Adler said he expects Stone Container to post a first-quarter loss of $0.75 a share and a full-year loss of $0.80 a share "assuming things start to improve in the spring."
Roger Stone declined to comment on market rumors that the company might sell Stone-Consolidated, in which it holds a 47 percent stake.
"We never comment on rumors," Stone said.
He called Stone-Consolidated, which produces publication papers, a "very important" holding and said "we think it's undervalued by the market."
